source: OIML R 76-2:2007 (E) — Non-automatic weighing instruments, Part 2: Test report format

derivedFrom.crossChecked: docs/standards/OIML_R76-2_2007_report_format.pdf (pages 9, 10, 12, 13, 16, 19, 20, 24, 25 rendered and visually compared to the extracted text)
derivedFrom.method: Manual read of the full 62-page extract, page by page, table by table. Column order, formulas and acceptance criteria were copied verbatim from the printed form. Pages with two-dimensional table layouts that the text extraction could mangle (7, 8, 12.x, 14) were additionally verified against the rendered PDF page images.

markingConvention.description: For each test, the SUMMARY OF TYPE EVALUATION and the CHECKLIST shall be completed according to this example (R 76-2 p.5, Explanatory notes):
markingConvention.verbatim: when the instrument has passed the test: X (in PASSED) / when the instrument has failed the test: X (in FAILED) / when the test is not applicable: – –

symbols.ΔL: Additional load to next changeover point
symbols.P: I + ½ e – ΔL = Indication prior to rounding (digital indication)
symbols.E: I – L  or  = P – L  or  = I + ½ e – ΔL – L  = Error

explanatoryNotes.unitsNote: The name(s) or symbol(s) of the unit(s) used to express test results shall be specified in each form.

environmentalHeaderExample.verbatim: The white spaces in boxes in the headings of the report should always be filled in according to the following example: At start / At max / At end — Temp.: 20.5 / (blank) / 21.2 °C ; Rel. h.: %; Time:; Bar. pres.: hPa

barometric pressure (necessary for the span stability test and when specified by IEC test provisions; in other cases it may be necessary only for class I instruments)

explanatoryNotes.dateNote: "Date" in the test report refers to the date on which the test was performed.
explanatoryNotes.disturbanceFaultNote: In the disturbance tests (12.1 through 12.7), faults greater than e are acceptable provided that they are detected and acted upon, or that they result from circumstances such that these faults shall not be considered as significant (see T.5.5.6 in R 76-1); an appropriate explanation shall be given in the column "Yes (remarks)".
explanatoryNotes.clauseReferenceNote: Numbers in brackets refer to the corresponding subclauses of OIML R 76-1.

summaryTable.title: Summary of type evaluation
notes: Row 1 (Weighing performance) has a sub-column 'Initial' plus 7 repeated '°C' lines, one per report page for a weighing-performance test that may be run at several temperatures/loads — each repetition is reported on its own page (see R 76-2 Introduction, p.4).
Row 7 (Stability of equilibrium) has two sub-rows: 'Printing, storage' and 'Zero-setting, tare balancing', matching the two/three sub-tables on form 7.
Rows 12.2, 12.3, 12.4, 12.7 and 13 have lettered sub-rows a)/b)/(c) that correspond 1:1 with the lettered sub-forms in this file.
Row 15 (Endurance) only lists sub-rows a) Initial test and c) Final test — b) Performance of the test is a procedural note, not a pass/fail item.
A row labelled 'EXAMINATIONS' (no data) separates the test rows (1–15) from rows 16–17.

forms.title: Repeatability
forms._kernelNote: This form is NOT listed under any kernel in CLAUDE.md §5. It uses the K1 error formula (E = I + 1/2 e – ΔL – L) but its acceptance criterion has two independent parts: a) E ≤ mpe (a K1-style check) AND b) Emax – Emin ≤ |mpe| (a spread/range check across 10 repeated weighings that no existing kernel in CLAUDE.md's table captures). Flagged for the team — see report.

environmental.pressureNote: Bar. pres. row marked '(only class I)'

formulas: E = I + 1/2 e – ΔL – L
forms.acceptance: Check if a) E ≤ mpe (3.6 of R 76-1); b) Emax – Emin ≤ absolute value of mpe (3.6.1 of R 76-1)
notes: Automatic zero-setting and zero-tracking device is: Non-existent / In operation (only two options on this form).
Table is split into two identical panels of 10 rows each: 'Load (weighing 1-10)' and 'Load (weighing 11-20)', each a fixed single load value entered once above its panel.
Emax – Emin and mpe are recorded separately for each of the two panels (weighing 1-10, weighing 11-20).

forms.title: Creep

environmental.pressureNote: Bar. pres. row marked '(only class I)'

formulas: P = I + ½ e – ΔL
ΔP = difference between P at the start (0 min) and P at a given time.
forms.acceptance: Check if condition a) or b) is fulfilled. a) ΔP ≤ 0.5 e after 30 minutes; and ΔP ≤ 0.2 e between the indication obtained at 15 minutes and that at 30 minutes. b) ΔP ≤ absolute value of mpe during the period of 4 hours
notes: * If condition a) is met, the test is terminated. If not, the test shall be continued for the next 3.5 hours and condition b) shall be met.

forms.title: Stability of equilibrium
forms._kernelNote: This form does NOT match K1's formula/acceptance pattern cleanly, and it is NOT listed under K1 in CLAUDE.md §5 at all. It has two independent checks, neither of which is 'error vs mpe from the resolver': (i) printing/storage — a fixed 1e deviation check on raw readings, no E/Ec computed; (ii) zero-setting/tare-balancing — uses the K1-shaped formula E0 = I0 + ½e – ΔL – L0 but checks against a FIXED 0.25e threshold, not the class/load-band mpe. CLAUDE.md's K4 row lists 'stability' as a K4 (time-dependence) user, but nothing on this form is time-based — that reference more likely means form 14 'Span stability', not this form. Flagged for the team — see report.

forms.title: Span stability
forms._kernelNote: Span stability's acceptance criterion is the ONLY one among the K1-tagged forms that does NOT reference 'mpe' at all — it is a graphical check of average error against fixed bands of ±0.5e / ±1e / ±1.5e ('Maximum allowable variation'), read directly off a plotted chart, not resolved via the class/load-band mpe resolver. This is a meaningful divergence from CLAUDE.md's description of K1 ('pass if |Ec| ≤ mpe') and from design rule #2 ('never hardcode a threshold') — here the standard's own form hardcodes the e-multiples. Flagged for the team — see report.

environmental._note: Header block repeats once per 'Measurement no. N' sub-section (there are at least 2, printed up to 8, with extension rows for more), not once for the whole form.

formulas: E0 = I0 + ½ e – ΔL0 – L0
EL = IL + ½ e – ΔL – L
forms.acceptance: No explicit 'Check if |Ec| ≤ mpe' line is printed on this form. Instead: (i) per measurement, 'If |(EL – E0)max – (EL – E0)min| ≤ 0.1 e, the loading and reading will be sufficient for each of the subsequent measurements; if not, five loadings and readings shall be performed at each measurement'; (ii) overall pass/fail is read from a plot of average error per measurement against 'Maximum allowable variation' bands of +1.5e, +1e, +0.5e, 0, –0.5e, –1e, –1.5e.
notes: Zero load and Test load recorded once at the top of the form.
Automatic span adjustment device: Existent / Non-existent; each measurement records whether it was activated.

Measurement no. 1 is the 'Initial measurement'; subsequent measurements (no. 2, 3, ... up to 8 shown, extensible) each record which condition triggered the re-measurement: after temperature test / after damp heat test / after disconnection from mains / after change in test location / other condition (free text).
'* When applicable, necessary corrections resulting from variations of temperature, pressure, etc. See remarks.'
Average error = average (EL – E0) computed for measurement 1 always; for subsequent measurements only if five loadings/readings were performed.

Final page: a graph plots the average error (y-axis, in bands of ±0.5e/±1e/±1.5e labelled 'Maximum allowable variation') against Measurement no. (x-axis, 1–8), with points marked T (temperature test), D (damp heat test), P (disconnection from mains). This page's text extraction is visually jumbled (Passed/Failed boxes and axis labels interleaved) — treated as _uncertain; the layout was inferred from context, not confirmed against the rendered PDF page for this specific page (45).
